english: Consider the four lines in the Argand plane
Then the area of the parallelogram bounded by $L_{1},L_{2},L_{3}$ and $L_{4}$ is
hindi: आर्गण्ड तल में चार रेखाओं पर विचार कीजिए
तब $L_{1},L_{2},L_{3}$ तथा $L_{4}$ द्वारा परिबद्ध समान्तर चतुर्भुज का क्षेत्रफल है
solution: $z\bar{a}+\bar{z}a+b=0$ is $2(a_{1}x+a_{2}y)+b=0$, at distance $\dfrac{|b|}{2|a|}$ from the origin; put each line in this form with the same $a$ for a parallel pair
solution_full: For $z=x+iy$ and $a=a_{1}+ia_{2}$, $z\bar{a}+\bar{z}a=2\,\mathrm{Re}(z\bar{a})=2(a_{1}x+a_{2}y)$. So $z\bar{a}+\bar{z}a+b=0$ is the line $2a_{1}x+2a_{2}y+b=0$ with normal along $a$.
$L_{2}$: $\bar{a}=2-4i$, $a=2+4i$, $b=-12$: $4x+8y-12=0$, i.e. $x+2y-3=0$. Same normal, so $L_{1}\parallel L_{2}$; the coefficient must be normalised before comparing constants.

The normals $(1,2)$ and $(3,-1)$ make an angle $\phi$ with $\cos\phi=\dfrac{3-2}{\sqrt{5}\sqrt{10}}=\dfrac{1}{5\sqrt{2}}$ and $\sin\phi=\dfrac{|1\cdot(-1)-2\cdot3|}{\sqrt{5}\sqrt{10}}=\dfrac{7}{5\sqrt{2}}$; the angle between the lines is the same.

A parallelogram whose opposite sides are at distances $d_{1}$ and $d_{2}$ and whose sides meet at angle $\phi$ has sides $\dfrac{d_{2}}{\sin\phi}$ and $\dfrac{d_{1}}{\sin\phi}$ and area $\dfrac{d_{1}}{\sin\phi}\cdot\dfrac{d_{2}}{\sin\phi}\cdot\sin\phi=\dfrac{d_{1}d_{2}}{\sin\phi}$.
(Using $\dfrac{|b|}{|a|}$ instead of $\dfrac{|b|}{2|a|}$ for the distances gives $20$; not normalising $L_{2}$ and $L_{4}$ gives $12$.)
originality_note: New: two parallel pairs given in the complex form with differently scaled coefficients; in this form the area reduces to |b1-b2||b3-b4|/(4|Im(a1 conj a2)|) (way 4, the moduli cancel). Closest known: distance between parallel lines in complex form; area of a parallelogram from four Cartesian lines. Different because: the pairs must first be recognised as parallel and normalised, and the angle comes from Im(conj(a) c).

concept_use.Straight line in complex form (z.a_bar +: Each line is read as 2(a1 x + a2 y) + b = 0; normalising a shows which lines are parallel and gives the angle between the normals.
concept_use.Distance of a point from a line, distanc: The widths d1 = sqrt5 and d2 = 7/sqrt10 of the two strips are distances between parallel lines; the area is d1 d2 / sin phi.

key_step: Normalise the scaled complex forms, get the two strip widths and the angle, then area = d1 d2 / sin phi.
justification: Routine pieces but with two traps (scaled coefficients, factor 2 in the distance) and the less common area formula d1 d2/sin phi; borderline 2-3, rated 3 because the options are built on exactly those slips. Near 2023-P1-Q16 (L3) for distance between lines.
